bbc.title: Nvidia shares slide as Trump's role in Jensen Huang's comeback questioned by US politicians
bbc.description: Nvidia's stock market value surged on the annoucement of Huang's reappointment, but some of the gains reversed in Tuesday trading.

bbc.title: What Jensen Huang's return teaches China's Xi about Trump
bbc.description: Huang being back at the helm of Nvidia is no guarantee of relief for Beijing.

bbc.title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports
bbc.description: German media said Russia planned to launch a satellite with a nuclear warhead into space in coming weeks.

bbc.title: Land mine casualties soar in Syria, two years after war
bbc.description: Nearly 1,000 children are among those killed or injured by explosives left over from the conflict, figures show.

bbc.title: Indian government has 'lost the plot', says 'cockroach' leader barred from UK flight
bbc.description: Saurav Das says immigration authorities at Delhi airport told him his passport had been flagged.

bbc.title: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
bbc.description: Naeem Abu Nahel, who had been in the post for two months, is among seven Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes on Tuesday.

bbc.title: French ex-President Sarkozy and wife Carla Bruni to face trial
bbc.description: It is the latest case involving Nicolas Sarkozy who became the first French ex-president to go to jail last year.

bbc.title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times
bbc.description: Published extracts from the late pontiff's diary claim one of the visions happened "in the choir loft" during Mass.

bbc.title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book
bbc.description: The publisher of an essay on coercive control apologises for "an unfortunate and inappropriate communication".

bbc.title: Zimbabwean convicted in South Africa of trying to fight in Ukraine
bbc.description: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.

bbc.title: Car bomb tears through Colombian city wounding more than 20
bbc.description: The explosion is the latest in a string of attacks on buildings housing the security forces and government offices.

bbc.title: DR Congo says military aircraft missing as rebels claim to shoot down plane
bbc.description: A South African fighter pilot and a Ugandan officer are reportedly among those aboard the downed plane.

bbc.title: Russian governor detained in rare criminal case against regional leader
bbc.description: Andrei Chibis, head of Russia's northern Murmansk region, is the first governor to be detained for five years.

bbc.title: Iranian authorities flog singer who performed without hijab, lawyers say
bbc.description: Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were reportedly given 74 lashes in Qom.

bbc.title: Bangladesh's ex-PM Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return on 16 December
bbc.description: Hasina has spoken several times of her desire to return, but this is the first time she has set a date.

bbc.title: Comedian impersonates Trump's dance moves, mocks trade talks at Canada press dinner
bbc.description: The impersonator, Canadian comedian Mark Critch, poked fun at the US president's search for a new press secretary and US-Canada trade talks.

bbc.title: King Charles and Elton John pay tribute to Australian music legend Molly Meldrum
bbc.description: The promoter and broadcaster helped define the music tastes of Australians for decades.

bbc.title: Watch: Moment troops raid home and capture Mexican drug lord
bbc.description: Newly-released bodycam footage shows the moment troops detained 'El Chapo Isidro', who had managed to evade capture for years.

rfi.title: Senegal reclaim Africa Cup of Nations title after 11-month legal fight
rfi.description: Judges at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Tuesday declared Senegal winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.

rfi.title: Police officer to stand trial for murder over shooting of French teenager Nahel
rfi.description: A French police officer who shot and killed 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk during a traffic stop in June 2023 will stand trial for murder following a ruling by an appeals court. Tuesday’s ruling is the latest in a series of competing judicial rulings over a case that has for many become a symbol of police brutality in France.

rfi.title: Gisèle Pelicot to file legal complaint against publisher over nude photo use
rfi.description: Gisèle Pelicot said on Monday she was "deeply shocked" that nude photographs of her had been used without her consent to promote a psychoanalyst's essay on the concept of coercive control.

rfi.title: France to establish 'strategic stockpiles' of critical minerals
rfi.description: France will build up "strategic stocks" of rare earths and certain priority metals, inspired by the reserves that exist for oil, the presidency announced on Monday.

rfi.title: Senegal or Morocco? Top sports lawyers to give verdict on 2025 AFCON champions
rfi.description: The ruling on who won the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final between Senegal and Morocco last January will be published on Tuesday, the Court of Arbitration for Sport has announced.

rfi.title: Zambia formally indicts opposition leader on treason charges
rfi.description: Zambian prosecutors have formally indicted the country's main opposition leader and 12 others on treason charges over an alleged plot to overthrow the government. This comes three months after a contested election which saw incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema secure a second term.

rfi.title: From the track to the gallery: Dakar's autumn in the spotlight
rfi.description: This November, Dakar hosted two exceptional events: the Youth Olympic Games, which ran until 13 November, and Dak'Art, the Dakar Biennale of contemporary African art, which runs from 19 November to 19 December. The Games were the first Olympic event ever held on the African continent, and the Biennale now brings together artists from across Africa and its diaspora. In this episode, we hear from participants in both events.

rfi.title: Macron pledges €350m for aviation research in a bid for industrial acceleration
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has announced €350 million in funding for civil aviation research and plans to create new industrial zones with simplified administrative procedures, as France looks to accelerate its re-industrialisation. The announcement came during the second Choose France business summit focused on the home market.

rfi.title: Zelensky calls for EU inclusion in talks with Russia 'as soon as possible'
rfi.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance.

rfi.title: UN condemns drone strikes in Khartoum suspected to have come from Ethiopia
rfi.description: A United Nations building was one of several structures damaged in drone attacks on Sudan’s capital, Khartoum, which are suspected to have been launched from Ethiopia.

rfi.title: Major cyberattack hits IT systems at Guadeloupe university hospital
rfi.description: A major cyberattack has disrupted the university hospital in the French overseas department of Guadeloupe, affecting its operations and forcing it to activate its emergency response plan and postpone non-emergency procedures.

rfi.title: French pair target Grand Slam glory after ATP Finals crown in Turin
rfi.description: French tennis players Théo Arribagé and Albano Olivetti were on Monday setting their sights on playing in their country's Davis Cup team and trophies at the four Grand Slam tournaments next year, after capturing the doubles title at the 2026 men's end of season championships.

rfi.title: France seeks fresh start with Israel as Lebanon peacekeeping deadline looms
rfi.description: France is hoping to rebuild relations with Israel's next government, as it steps up efforts to secure a new security arrangement for southern Lebanon before the United Nations peacekeeping mission there ends its operations in December.

rfi.title: UN warns Libya must not become stage for Russia-Ukraine war after drone strikes
rfi.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said his country was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow's war with Kyiv. The United Nations condemned Sunday's strikes and has called for an international investigation.

rfi.title: Cop31 climate talks collapse as EU rejects deal that omits fossil fuels
rfi.description: The Cop31 climate summit in Turkey has ended in disarray after the European Union and several other countries rejected a proposed global agreement that failed to explicitly mention fossil fuels. The breakdown, after more than two weeks of negotiations and a record 44 hours of overtime, marks a major setback for international climate diplomacy, with deep divisions over energy policy and financial support for developing nations left unresolved.

rfi.title: French right backs Macron's plan to put public spending limits in constitution
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron is reportedly considering a constitutional reform to curb public deficits, with right-wing parties and the far-right National Rally signalling their willingness to support the move. The proposal could bring MPs and senators together for a vote as early as January, months before the 2027 presidential election.

rfi.title: EU proposes digital companies tax as France and Germany clash over cuts
rfi.description: The European Union has unveiled plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to help finance its next long-term budget, as Brussels seeks to overcome deep divisions between member states over spending priorities. The proposal has already drawn criticism from France and Germany.

rfi.title: Nepal's first United Nations climate loss and damage payout falls short
rfi.description: Nepal is set to become the first country to receive money from the United Nations Loss and Damage Fund following devastating floods in August. But the provisional €19 million allocation covers less than 1 percent of the damage – and survivors are still waiting for help.

euronews.title: At least 24 injured after car bomb detonates in central Colombia
euronews.description: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella arrived in Villavicencio at around 9 am local time on Tuesday as he prepared to hold a security meeting and visit the scene of the blast.

euronews.title: Matryoshka: What is the Russian disinformation campaign targeting Spain's election?
euronews.description: Spain is heading to the polls this weekend, in an election marred by disinformation online. With France, Italy and Poland also holding elections in the coming months, how prepared is Europe to deal with a new wave of fake political news?

euronews.title: Indonesia names former police chief as treason suspect in presidential wiretapping case
euronews.description: An investigation into alleged surveillance of Indonesia’s president has widened into a treason case against senior police figures. It has already led to dismissals and parliamentary scrutiny, with police alleging a plot to undermine Prabowo’s government.

euronews.title: Pope Francis' private notes reveal visions of the devil and a plan to allow married men to be priests
euronews.description: The book published on Tuesday contains Jorge Mario Bergoglio's notes over 30 years, including meetings with the devil, a spiritual crisis, and his choice on married priests.

euronews.title: Europe Tonight: EU budget battle, €45B Ukraine aid, and Serbia-Kosovo tensions
euronews.description: Europe Tonight unpacks the fierce clash in Brussels over the EU’s next seven-year budget and a proposed €45 billion loan package for Ukraine, examines Serbia-Kosovo diplomatic tensions ahead of the Western Balkans summit with former Kosovo President Vjosa Osmani, and features an exclusive interview

euronews.title: Latest news bulletin | November 24th, 2026 – Evening
euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 24th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: UK warns defence suppliers to Ukraine over Russian sabotage
euronews.description: The warning follows a fresh wave of security incidents across Europe in recent weeks, including airspace violations and reported cyber and sabotage attacks.

euronews.title: New terms and conditions: Tidal bans AI music in a bid to promote fairness in industry
euronews.description: The streaming giant says its begun moves to ban and remove up to 29 million AI generated tracks from its platform in a decision it predicts will be welcomed by artists and fans alike.

euronews.title: MEPs call on the Commission to assess human rights in Rwanda amid return hub plans
euronews.description: The letter signed by 76 MEPs targets a controversial plan to set up a centre in Rwanda for migrants with no legal right to stay in Europe.

euronews.title: Italy watches worryingly as Ukraine strikes Russian boats in Libya
euronews.description: Ukraine's naval drone strikes on two Russian vessels in and off Benghazi have alarmed Italy, amid fears that the attacks could reignite Libya's civil war.

euronews.title: Colombia: At least 25 injured in bombing as armed violence resurges
euronews.description: At least 25 people were injured in a bombing in Villavicencio, damaging government buildings, businesses and vehicles. Meanwhile, hundreds of residents marched with candles in Cúcuta following a separate attack, amid a resurgence of armed violence in Colombia.

euronews.title: Italy develops 'ambitious' business with 'strategic partner' Azerbaijan, Tajani tells Euronews
euronews.description: Italy's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told Euronews that Rome has sought to expand its business relations with Baku now that peace has brought stability and improved connectivity to the region.

euronews.title: Two arrested on suspicion of burglary at Prince and Princess of Wales' UK country home
euronews.description: Two men were arrested on the Sandringham estate on suspicion of burglary and trespass and remain in custody, Norfolk Police said. The force added that the property was unoccupied at the time of the incident.

euronews.title: Why French pharma firm Sanofi is paying $41 billion for US company Insmed
euronews.description: French drugmaker Sanofi has agreed a $41 billion (€37.4bn) all-cash takeover of Insmed, a US biopharma company. The deal, one of its biggest ever, is meant to refill its pipeline of new medicines before its best-selling drug loses patent protection.

euronews.title: ‘Pervert glasses’ named Word of the Year by Macquarie dictionary
euronews.description: The Australian dictionary’s committee of word experts said the winning term is "a succinct reflection of the state of the world in 2026". 'Pervert glasses' follows ‘enshittification’ in 2024 and ‘AI slop’ in 2025.

euronews.title: Visegrad leaders demand delay to ETS2, piling pressure on EU's carbon market
euronews.description: Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic want to soften the bloc's expanded carbon market ahead of the 26-27 November European Council

euronews.title: Migrant caravans head north through Mexico towards US border
euronews.description: Migrants from several Central American countries are travelling through southern Mexico in a caravan, hoping to reach the United States.

euronews.title: Senegal reinstated as AFCON champions as Morocco vows to fight on
euronews.description: The sport's top court ruled that the referee's decision to restart the final after Senegal's walk-off could not be challenged, while Morocco has raised questions over alleged contact between one of the judges and Senegal's federation.

lemonde.title: Derrière l’affaire Nvidia, un vaste réseau de détournement de puces d’IA au service de la Chine
lemonde.description: Alors que Jensen Huang a repris la tête du géant des processeurs américain, lundi 23 novembre, la presse financière mondiale retrace les méthodes qui ont permis d’expédier les puces vers le territoire chinois, malgré les restrictions des Etats-Unis.

lemonde.title: Hackers et médias révèlent ce que le Kremlin voulait cacher : le bilan de 500 000 morts au moins sur le front ukrainien
lemonde.description: Depuis que les troupes russes ont envahi l’Ukraine en février 2022, Vladimir Poutine a empêché la publication des chiffres de décès. Mais des hackers ont piraté les registres de l’agence de statistiques. Et des médias en exil ont passé au crible les données. Le décompte dépasserait les 700 000 morts, en incluant les militaires disparus.

lemonde.title: Nicolas Sarkozy, Carla Bruni et Mimi Marchand renvoyés devant le tribunal dans l’affaire de la fausse rétractation de l’homme d’affaires Ziad Takieddine
lemonde.description: L’ancien chef de l’Etat comparaîtra fin 2027 devant les juges pour « participation à association de malfaiteurs en vue de commettre une escroquerie en bande organisée » et « recel de subornation de témoin ». Les juges le soupçonnent d’avoir participé à la rétractation impromptue et médiatisée de l’un de ses principaux accusateurs dans l’enquête sur le financement libyen présumé de sa campagne présidentielle de 2007, Ziad Takieddine.

lemonde.title: La difficile quête de souveraineté de la filière drones, dépendante de composants critiques chinois
lemonde.description: Moteurs, batteries, hélices… De nombreux appareils, y compris destinés à des usages militaires, ne peuvent pas voler sans ces pièces produites en Chine. Les industriels cherchent à développer une filière européenne pour viser l’indépendance.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Edouard Philippe a voté pour David Lisnard à la présidence de l’AMF, mais fustige sa posture dans la course à l’Elysée
lemonde.description: Le candidat Horizons a rapproché au maire de Cannes de vouloir travailler avec la droite et la « droite extrême ». De son côté, le candidat Nouvelle Energie s’est engagé à continuer « à défendre les mairies » s’il était élu à l’Elysée.

lemonde.title: « Paper Tiger » : le cinéaste James Gray livre le récit captivant d’une lente dislocation familiale
lemonde.description: Le nouveau film du réalisateur américain, présenté en compétition à Cannes et inspiré de sa propre jeunesse, est servi par un formidable trio d’acteurs, Scarlett Johansson, Adam Driver et Miles Teller.

lemonde.title: En Colombie, prise d’otages lors du braquage d’un supermarché à Carthagène, au lendemain d’un attentat à la voiture piégée à Villavicencio
lemonde.description: Cette attaque intervient le jour du dixième anniversaire d’un accord de paix historique entre l’Etat colombien et la guérilla des Forces armées révolutionnaires de Colombie.

lemonde.title: Fuites du ministère de l’intérieur vers le RN : Laurent Nuñez dit avoir proposé un successeur au préfet Hugues Moutouh
lemonde.description: L’ancien haut fonctionnaire du ministère de l’intérieur est soupçonné d’avoir joué un rôle dans la transmission au Rassemblement national d’informations confidentielles sur les enquêtes visant le parti.

lemonde.title: Chez SFR, les ventes continuent de chuter en pleine opération de rachat par Bouygues Telecom, Free et Orange
lemonde.description: Le groupe de Patrick Drahi a fait état d’une baisse de son chiffre d’affaires de près de 8 % au troisième trimestre, et a choisi de ne plus publier son nombre d’abonnés.

lemonde.title: « La vérité d’une rencontre s’établit sur le terrain » : le Sénégal, déclaré vainqueur près d’un an après la finale contre le Maroc, célèbre son titre de champion d’Afrique
lemonde.description: La finale de la CAN 2025 entre le Sénégal et le Maroc s’était achevée, le 18 janvier, dans la tension, ouvrant la voie à des mois de batailles juridiques. Mardi 24 novembre, le Tribunal arbitral du sport a déclaré vainqueurs les Lions de la Teranga.

lemonde.title: Eric Zemmour définitivement condamné pour avoir affirmé que le maréchal Pétain « avait sauvé les juifs français »
lemonde.description: La Cour de cassation a jugé que ses propos tenus sur CNews en 2019 constituaient une « une minoration outrancière de la Shoah telle qu’elle a été mise en œuvre sur le territoire français ».

lemonde.title: Alcool : l’expérimentation en hausse chez les collégiens et les lycéens, les autres usages régressent, y compris chez les adultes
lemonde.description: Le bilan annuel que l’Observatoire français des drogues et des tendances addictives consacre à la consommation d’alcool et ses conséquences, publié mardi 24 novembre, acte l’augmentation de la tendance à tester des boissons alcoolisées chez les jeunes scolarisés, après plus de dix ans de baisse.

lemonde.title: Budget 2027 : la fonction publique ciblée par la droite et le centre au Sénat
lemonde.description: Fidèle à la ligne qu’elle affiche depuis plusieurs années, la majorité sénatoriale avance plusieurs pistes d’économies visant les fonctionnaires. Elle veut notamment réformer le supplément familial de traitement, ce complément de rémunération versé aux agents ayant au moins un enfant.

lemonde.title: Ligue des champions : à l’exception du PSG, les clubs de football français évoluent « dans la deuxième division européenne »
lemonde.description: Les performances décevantes de Lens et de Lille dans la prestigieuse compétition, dont la cinquième journée commence mardi 24 novembre, éclairent les difficultés financières des clubs de Ligue 1, contraints de vendre leurs meilleurs joueurs pour compenser l’effondrement des revenus issus des droits télévisuels.

lemonde.title: Assurance-vie : que penser des fonds euros nouvelle génération ?
lemonde.description: Trois familles de produits, aux fonctionnements bien spécifiques, ciblant davantage de rendement, sont apparues, moyennant une plus grande sophistication de leur moteur de performance.

lemonde.title: Ikea cherche la parade face à l’effritement du marché de la maison
lemonde.description: L’enseigne va poursuivre des campagnes massives de baisse de tarifs et tester l’implantation de grands espaces de « seconde chance » pour séduire les consommateurs à la recherche de prix cassés.

france24fr.description: Le Tribunal arbitral du sport a finalement tranché : déboutant le jury d'appel de la CAF qui avait déchu le Sénégal du titre de la CAN 2025, l'instance suisse lui a rendu sa couronne. Du Maroc au siège de la confédération africaine, les réactions affluent à la suite de cette décision historique.

france24fr.title: IA : les femmes occupent majoritairement les emplois les plus menacés
france24fr.description: Les emplois de bureau peu qualifiés sont "en première ligne" face à l'intelligence artificielle, ce qui pourrait affecter beaucoup plus les femmes, selon une note d'économistes publiée mardi.

france24fr.title: Colombie : une prise d'otages est en cours dans la ville touristique de Carthagène
france24fr.description: Une trentaine de personnes ont été prises en otage mardi dans un supermarché de la ville touristique de Carthagène. Sur les réseaux sociaux, des vidéos montrent des personnes agenouillées à l'intérieur du bâtiment. Des dizaines de policiers et tireurs d'élite ont été déployés autour du supermarché.

france24fr.title: Mort de Nahel : la réaction de la famille après le pourvoi en cassation du policier mis en cause
france24fr.description:
Le 27 juin 2023, Nahel Merzouk, 17 ans, est tué à Nanterre, dans les Hauts-de-Seine, d'une balle tirée à bout portant par le policier Florian M. lors d'un contrôle routier. La scène, filmée, devient virale sur les réseaux sociaux. Plusieurs nuits de violences secouent la France.

france24fr.title: Plus de 700 000 soldats russes morts en Ukraine : ce que l'on sait de cette nouvelle estimation
france24fr.description: À partir d'une fuite de données de l'agence russe des statistiques, les médias indépendants Meduza et Mediazona estiment à plus de 700 000 le nombre de militaires russes morts depuis février 2022, selon une nouvelle enquête publiée lundi. France 24 fait le point sur ce que l'on sait.

france24fr.title: CAN 2025 : pourquoi le TAS a donné raison à l'arbitre et au Sénégal
france24fr.description: Le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) a invalidé, mardi, la décision du jury d'appel de la CAF et rendu au Sénégal son titre de champion d'Afrique 2025 face au Maroc. L'instance basée à Lausanne estime que l'arbitre de la finale était seul juge pour reprendre la partie après l'interruption provoquée par les Lions de la Teranga.

france24fr.title: David Lisnard, le candidat ultralibéral qui chamboule la campagne à droite
france24fr.description: Le président de l'Association des maires de France, David Lisnard, est le candidat surprise de la droite à l'élection présidentielle. Issu du parti Les Républicains, il est entré en campagne au printemps malgré la désignation par les adhérents de Bruno Retailleau comme candidat. Avec ses positions très libérales, il devance désormais ce dernier dans les sondages, mais aussi Gabriel Attal et même Édouard Philippe.

france24fr.title: Protection des forêts : les peuples autochtones veulent peser dans les décisions
france24fr.description: Ils veulent faire entendre leurs voix dans le tumulte du monde. Réunis à Paris pour un premier sommet international qui leur est consacré, les peuples autochtones entendent faire reconnaître leurs droits et leur rôle dans la préservation de la biodiversité. Au cœur des discussions : la protection des forêts, avec un objectif ambitieux de 10 millions d'hectares à préserver. france24fr.title: Sénégal vainqueur de la CAN : fin du feuilleton ?
france24fr.description: Le Tribunal arbitral du sport confirme le sacre du Sénégal lors de la Coupe d'Afrique des nations 2025, aux dépens du Maroc qui avait obtenu le titre sur tapis vert. La fédération marocaine indique qu'elle engagera "toutes les procédures légales nécessaires" contre la décision du TAS. Page spéciale.

france24fr.title: 🔴En direct : le Maroc veut utiliser "tous les recours légaux possibles" après la décision du TAS en faveur du Sénégal
CAN 2025 : le Sénégal, vainqueur officiel selon le verdict du TAS
france24fr.description: Le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) a décidé mardi "à l'unanimité" le sacre du Sénégal lors de la Coupe d'Afrique des nations 2025, aux dépens du Maroc qui avait obtenu le titre sur tapis vert. Le Maroc dispose de 30 jours pour faire appel de la décision devant le Tribunal fédéral suisse.

france24fr.title: Boxe : la championne olympique Imane Khelif de retour sur le ring
france24fr.description: Depuis le 9 août 2024, date à laquelle Imane Khelif a remporté la médaille d'or en boxe féminine aux Jeux olympiques, la boxeuse s'était éloignée des rings. Et pour cause, l'athlète algérienne avait été la cible d'une virulente campagne de cyberharcèlement et d'attaques infondées remettant en cause son genre. La boxeuse s'apprête à remonter sur le ring ce 15 décembre, pour son premier combat professionnel.

france24fr.description: Le Tribunal arbitral du sport confirme le sacre du Sénégal lors de la Coupe d'Afrique des nations 2025, aux dépens du Maroc qui avait obtenu le titre sur tapis vert. france24fr.title: Fausse rétractation de Takieddine : renvoi en procès de Nicolas Sarkozy et Carla Bruni
france24fr.description: L'ancien président de la République Nicolas Sarkozy, son épouse Carla Bruni-Sarkozy et la "papesse des paparazzis" "Mimi" Marchand seront jugés en 2027 dans l'affaire de la rétractation possiblement monnayée de l'intermédiaire Ziad Takieddine, a appris l'AFP mardi de source proche du dossier, confirmant une information de RTL.

france24fr.title: CAN-2025: le Sénégal récupère son titre, le Maroc déchu (TAS)

france24fr.title: Détournement de fonds de publics : une enquête vise l'agglomération du Havre d'Édouard Philippe
france24fr.description: Nouvelle péripétie judiciaire pour le candidat à l'élection présidentielle Édouard Philippe : une enquête a été ouverte à la suite d'un signalement à la justice pour détournement de fonds publics à la communauté urbaine du Havre, qu'il dirige. Également placé sous statut de témoin assisté dans une autre procédure menée par le parquet national financier, l'ex-Premier ministre dénonce une "vendetta judiciaire".

france24fr.title: Verdict du TAS : existe-t-il un recours pour le Maroc ?
france24fr.description: Le Tribunal arbitral du sport basé à Lausanne, en Suisse, a déclaré mardi le Sénégal vainqueur de la CAN 2025. Après cette décision de justice, le Maroc a-t-il encore des recours alors qu'il dit vouloir recourir à toutes les "possibilités légales" ? France 24 fait le point.

france24fr.title: Mort de Nahel : la justice confirme en appel le renvoi du policier pour meurtre
france24fr.description: Trois ans après la mort de Nahel Merzouk, la cour d'appel de Versailles a ordonné mardi que le policier soit jugé devant la cour d'assises des Hauts-de-Seine pour meurtre, une décision contestée par la défense, qui annonce se pourvoir en cassation.

spiegel.description: Manuel Neuer soll sich von seiner Partnerin getrennt haben – und die Paarberaterin Ruth Marquardt geht mit einem emotionalen Video viral. Hier sagt sie, warum der Fall so viele Menschen berührt.

spiegel.description: Westliche Geheimdienste gehen wohl davon aus, dass Russland zeitnah einen Atomsprengkopf ins All bringen könnte. Die deutschen Streitkräfte würden in diesem Fall die Mittel »Stören, Blenden und Hacken« setzen.

spiegel.title: Olaf Scholz im Live-Gespräch: Was ist Deutschlands Rolle in der neuen Krisen-Welt?
spiegel.description: Krieg in der Ukraine und Donald Trump im Weißen Haus: Was heißt das für unsere Außenpolitik? Darüber spricht SPIEGEL-Korrespondentin Britta Sandberg mit SPD-Altkanzler Olaf Scholz auf dem Foreign Policy Forum der Körber-Stiftung.

spiegel.title: Gisèle Pelicot: Verlag wirbt mit Nacktbildern für antifeministischen Essay
spiegel.description: Alles nicht so einfach mit den Tätern und Opfern, behauptet eine französische Psychoanalytikerin in einem Buch. Der Verlag garniert die PR-Kampagne mit intimen Fotos Gisèle Pelicots. Die Rechtfertigung ist mehr als fadenscheinig.

phys-org.title: Selective logging can better preserve subtropical forest adaptive capacity than clear-cutting
phys-org.description: Adaptive capacity—the ability to cope with disturbances and environmental change—offers a useful perspective for sustainable forest management. However, applying this concept to logging remains challenging, and a key question is how different logging practices affect forest adaptive capacity.

phys-org.title: Biologists sort bacteria-killing peptides by speed: Slow is smooth, smooth is more effective
phys-org.description: A quick kill is not always best when battling bacterial infections. Sometimes, as new Stanford research shows, slower is better.

phys-org.title: Birds respond more quickly to predators in habitats with greater species diversity
phys-org.description: The diversity of species in a habitat is a common focus of conservation efforts. Local biodiversity has been shown to influence important ecosystem functions like pollination and pest control. In this study, Kumar and colleagues investigated the impact of diversity on the flow of ecological information in the form of defensive bird calls.

phys-org.title: New system enables highly sensitive detection of trace hydrogen
phys-org.description: A research team led by professor Fang Yonghua at the Hefei Institutes of Physical Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences has developed a new system for detecting trace amounts of hydrogen that improves detection sensitivity by reducing background interference, enabling it to directly detect hydrogen at a concentration of one part per million (ppm).

phys-org.title: A unified framework for carbon dioxide removal—with an ocean view
phys-org.description: When it comes to reducing atmospheric carbon, most roads lead to the sea. That's only natural, since the ocean is Earth's largest accessible repository for CO₂. Even without interventions to enhance its ability to capture carbon, the ocean holds about 50 times more carbon than the atmosphere and more than 20 times more carbon than plants, animals and soil combined.

phys-org.title: Getting blood out of bone
phys-org.description: "Jurassic Park" gave us a mosquito in amber, dinosaur DNA and a fantastic argument against opening a theme park. No mosquitoes were needed for this recent discovery, because the dinosaur fossil preserved its own bloody evidence of a land before time.

phys-org.title: New theoretical model allows for sustained entanglement between diamond qubits at greater separations
phys-org.description: In a new study accepted in the journal Physical Review B, a team of physicists from the University of Delaware may have found a way to overcome limitations in maintaining the entanglement of diamond qubits. The model involves driving the qubits away from equilibrium using microwave radiation while the surrounding material is allowed to remain in equilibrium. The approach allows for both long-range and steady-state entanglement of the qubits. The paper is published on the arXiv preprint server.

phys-org.title: Simple 'grow-and-repel' rule explains how brain immune cells organize themselves to protect nervous tissue
phys-org.description: Imagine you need to cover a large territory with trees, ensuring no gaps are left. What is the most efficient way to plant them? This is the spatial puzzle faced by microglia, the immune cells of our brain. During development, these cells must spread across the nervous tissue to monitor and protect, yet there is no central coordinator: each cell senses only its immediate surroundings.

phys-org.title: New research reveals a bias in employee reference checks
phys-org.description: When managers are asked to provide a reference for an employee, they may be doing more than describing that person's performance. They may also be promoting themselves.

phys-org.title: Four decades of citizen science reveal widespread declines in native plant distributions in Japan
phys-org.description: A new study led by researchers at Kyushu University has found that nearly 45% of 1,864 native plant species surveyed across Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan, were recorded in fewer locations over approximately four decades. The findings, published in Communications Biology on Sept. 15, 2026, show how long-running citizen science surveys can reveal biodiversity changes that conventional assessments focused on threatened species may miss.

phys-org.title: Tiny tracker reveals the longest ever recorded hummingbird migration
phys-org.description: Small though they may be, hummingbirds are no slouches when it comes to long-distance flight. These tiny birds can migrate thousands of miles across countries and continents. And now researchers have revealed the longest hummingbird migration to date—an impressive 6,526-kilometer journey (4,055 miles) from Alabama to Alaska in just 38 days.

phys-org.title: Ice near Antarctica's surface could unlock climate clues millions of years old
phys-org.description: Some of the oldest clues to Earth's climate history lie surprisingly close to Antarctica's surface. Researchers at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) are exploring the potential of these ancient archives, with a new scientific perspective coinciding with two Antarctic field expeditions.

phys-org.title: Water signals could guide future efforts to image supermassive black hole shadows
phys-org.description: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa researchers are exploring a new way to study some of the universe's most mysterious objects: supermassive black holes.

phys-org.title: Having fun learning with an app like Duolingo? You might be learning less than you think
phys-org.description: Apps like Duolingo aim to make learning as enjoyable as possible. But enjoyment can also make you feel you are learning more than you actually are. This is the finding of research by Tilburg marketing researchers Robert Smith and Anna Paley. In an experiment with a language-learning app, participants who completed a more enjoyable learning task believed that they learned more than they actually did. The study is published in the Journal of Marketing Research.

phys-org.title: Deep-sea clam discovered living inside the throat of a sea urchin
phys-org.description: A new species of bivalve has been discovered living inside the esophagus of a deep-sea urchin in one of the most unusual partnerships known among clams. Named Vaticinaria gulicola, it was found on the abyssal seafloor of the Great Australian Bight, at depths of about 4,000 to 5,000 meters (13,100 to 16,400 feet).

phys-org.title: Designing and optimizing genetic circuits in biology
phys-org.description: Although genetic circuits are important tools in synthetic biology and related fields, such as health care and sustainable manufacturing, designing them to function reliably can be challenging and often requires extensive laboratory testing and optimization.

phys-org.title: Four radiation belts surrounded Earth for weeks after 2024 solar superstorm
phys-org.description: Within Earth's magnetic field, energetic particles are trapped in two doughnut-shaped regions known as the Van Allen radiation belts—usually separated by a gap where particles are especially sparse. This structure can be dramatically rearranged during solar storms, but until now, astronomers have remained largely unsure as to how this happens.

phys-org.title: Offshore wind turbine hum may make phytoplankton grow faster
phys-org.description: They are single-celled, tiny and vital to life on Earth. Phytoplankton, which drift freely in the water column, provide food and oxygen for other marine organisms, while consuming CO₂ and nutrients—much like plants on land.

undark.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Has Not Worked — For Now
undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

proj-syn.title: Holiday 2026 Reading List
proj-syn.description: In the bi-weekly PS Book Recommendations newsletter—available for free to all registered PS readers—we highlight insightful, informative, or otherwise compelling books, written or recommended by PS contributors. Here, we present a selection of recent works by PS contributors that are worth adding to your holiday shopping list (and your bookshelf).

proj-syn.title: The Summit of Self-Promotion
proj-syn.description: Despite claiming that world history was made in Shenzhen with the US–Russia–China Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, the trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump, and Vladimir Putin was about optics, not substance. One of the many important problems they failed to address was China’s export-led growth.

proj-syn.title: Why Nvidia Couldn’t Quit Jensen Huang
proj-syn.description: Developing AI requires tremendous coordination across firms and sectors, from the AI labs themselves to energy and computing infrastructure, as well as long-term vision and patience. Whereas much of this coordination and planning is led by the government in China, in the US, it has been driven largely by one CEO.

proj-syn.title: Chips Too Big to Fail
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration pushed for Jensen Huang to be reinstated as CEO of Nvidia to keep the stock market high, to feed a possible productivity surge, and to advance a US foreign policy built on reconciliation with China. But will Americans continue to believe in the AI miracle and this new version of Chimerica?

proj-syn.title: Amplifying the Voice of Human Limits
proj-syn.description: Tech leaders like Elon Musk have embraced Prometheus as a symbol of creation, conquest, and discovery. But the Promethean impulse must be balanced by the “Orphic” tradition’s respect for and contemplation of nature’s mystery.

proj-syn.title: Making the Most of South Korea’s Semiconductor Boom
proj-syn.description: The AI boom has driven South Korea’s economic growth well above expectations, thanks to soaring demand for advanced semiconductors. But AI’s transformative potential does not guarantee that the current investment frenzy will continue, leaving the economy vulnerable to a downturn.

proj-syn.title: Is a Financial-Market Reckoning Imminent?
proj-syn.description: After a year of unprecedented AI investment, increasingly financed by debt in opaque private markets, growing unease about the industry’s future is reflected in sharp declines in the NASDAQ index and the S&P 500. But the stock market’s dependence on a handful of highly leveraged companies—and even a single CEO—is hardly the only source of global financial risk. Amid mounting fears, we asked PS contributors what to expect from financial markets in the year ahead.

proj-syn.title: The African Union’s Elusive Quest for Security
proj-syn.description: The African Union has long sought to implement Ali Mazrui’s concept of Pax Africana, but has faced persistent logistical and financial constraints. The key to making peacekeeping operations more effective is establishing a better division of labor between the AU, the United Nations, and regional African organizations.

proj-syn.title: The Achilles’ Heel of Emerging Economies’ Trade
proj-syn.description: New research shows that 23% of global goods imports in 2024 faced at least two of three vulnerabilities: product criticality, supply concentration, and geopolitical distance. Given the wide range of problems, early diagnosis and targeted action are particularly important for emerging economies with limited fiscal space.

proj-syn.title: AI Agents Could Make Big Tech Bigger
proj-syn.description: The rise of agentic AI could give a handful of Big Tech firms unprecedented power over our personal lives. Unless lawmakers and regulators act now, these digital gatekeepers could manipulate consumers, turbocharge corporate surveillance, and threaten our individual rights and civil liberties.

proj-syn.title: If the AI Bubble Is Bursting, the Fallout Will Be Severe
proj-syn.description: With the S&P 500 following the tech-heavy NASDAQ into correction territory, even as Anthropic set a record with its initial public offering, this is a good moment to compare AI stock valuations with earlier asset-price bubbles. A look back at the dot-com boom and bust of the late 1990s offers ample cause for concern.

proj-syn.title: Journalism Can Be More Than AI Fodder
proj-syn.description: As AI fundamentally alters the information environment, news publishers risk becoming little more than content suppliers for Big Tech. To avoid that fate, many are drawing on their archives and expertise to develop AI tools that allow them to operate and compete on their own terms.

proj-syn.title: Governing African Economies as They Are
proj-syn.description: Africa cannot overcome its development challenges by applying the same knowledge, economic, and innovation systems that helped create them. Imagining and governing new ways forward will require three intellectual ruptures.

proj-syn.title: Making Earth Cool Again
proj-syn.description: Climate multilateralism is evolving into a two-tiered system in which high-level negotiations toward shared commitments and the real-world implementation of climate solutions become more mutually supportive. Only by unleashing such virtuous cycles can we keep the 1.5ºC target for global warming within reach.

proj-syn.title: America’s Lame-Duck Autocrat
proj-syn.description: When autocrats suffer a defeat, they tend to double down, such as by intensifying repression at home or behaving more recklessly abroad. With two years left in office after historic midterm election losses, this is the road US President Donald Trump appears to be taking.

proj-syn.title: Getting Ukraine’s House in Order
proj-syn.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly opposed the idea of forming a national unity government. But bringing opposition leaders into the cabinet would ensure the checks on corruption and wayward bureaucratic action that Zelensky’s team can no longer provide.

proj-syn.title: What Adam Smith Missed
proj-syn.description: For all that he got right, the "founding father" of economics failed to see how technological innovations lead to market monopolization. If AI is left to the invisible hand, it will almost certainly increase economic and political inequality, causing even deeper social polarization and further undermining democracy.

proj-syn.title: China Ratchets Up Its Weaponization of Trade
proj-syn.description: Just as the US has been leveraging its large market and technological leadership for geopolitical ends, China is now using its dominance in critical minerals, industrial inputs, and specialized manufacturing machinery to coerce and punish other countries. The consequences, both economic and geopolitical, are far-reaching.
